correctness.rationale: The exact fixed-point equation rearranges to a(b-a^2)=c(c-1)(c+1). For c>=2, each positive divisor a uniquely determines an integer base; the proof separately verifies b>a and b>c, so the parametrization is genuinely bijective. Fixed-leading-digit admissibility is the congruence a|c(c-1)(c+1). Odd prime powers have exactly the residues 0,±1; powers of 2 have local counts 2,3,5 for exponents 1,2,>=3. CRT yields the density formula. The packaged checker independently verifies all three layers.

value.rationale: Cubic digit fixed points are a standard generalized-happy-number object with published finite-base censuses. The theorem replaces the complete two-digit portion of those scattered examples by an unrestricted normal form across all bases. The exact tau(c^3-c) fiber count and the multiplicative CRT density for fixed leading digit expose nontrivial divisor structure and provide reusable invariants beyond a routine verification of individual examples.
